rationale: Use Medicare as a national policy benchmark for equitable access to clinically indicated care in later life, when chronic illness and per-person healthcare use are substantial. Compare coverage, payment and access with clinical need across shared systems and reproductive anatomy/physiology.
age_rule: Emphasize later-life care without excluding younger Medicare beneficiaries. Analyze ages 65–74, 75–84 and 85+ when reported; distinguish under-65 beneficiaries and disability, ESRD or ALS entitlement where available. Preserve mixed-age studies with explicit applicability limits.
measurement_rule: Separate per-person utilization, spending, unmet need and share of national spending. Cross-sectional age comparisons do not establish a lifetime share of care or isolate aging as the cause. Medicare enrollment is not an age variable, and Medicare policy is not a universal measure of clinical appropriateness.
comparison_rule: For sex comparisons, retain age distribution, clinical need, severity, follow-up/person-time and mortality where available. Present crude and age-standardized or stratified results when justified. Prespecify adjustment for disease burden, disability and care setting; do not automatically remove potential mechanisms of inequity.
